newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU gas oil stock build introduces bearish tinge.
newsitem.headline: EU gas oil stock build introduces bearish tinge.

text.p: A second monthly build of European gas oil stocks has surprised some in the market and, say analysts, has introduced a bearish tinge to product prices heading into winter.
"Quite clearly the figures are bearish as they do show some spare capacity in heating oil that may be required in the next month," said Keith Hamm of Petroleum Economics.

Middle distillate stocks in the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose 2.55 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in November to 295.73 million barrels, Stichting Euroilstock said in its monthly report published on Tuesday.
The build wiped out the year-on-year shortfall that has persisted for most of the year. Distillate stocks were 770,000 barrels higher than at the end of November 1995.
Analysts and traders had generally expected gas oil stocks to be steady to slightly up, but not a build of this size.
At 1630 GMT, December IPE gas oil was trading down $1 a tonne at $214.50. IPE brokers said the substantial build of European stocks helped to push gas oil futures from its highs.
However, the easing of supply should not make buyers complacent as worldwide demand for distillates continues to grow.

"From a security point of view there is perhaps a need to have higher inventories. The fear is that as demand grows, the inventories are not keeping up," said Peter Bogin of Cambridge Energy Research Associates.
Bogin said Asian demand for oil products as a whole has risen 4 million barrels per day in the last five years, making oil products more vulnerable and volatile than before.

The distillate build was made possible by a dramatic rise in the crude input into European refineries. Crude intake rose 640,000 barrels per day in November and capacity utilisation was up from 87.37 percent to 92.41. Crude stocks also rose by 6.35 million barrels during the same period.
Analysts say the rise in input was mainly the result of large inflows of West African crudes. Production in the North Sea did not rise dramatically in November, they say.
The record November IPE gas oil delivery may also have played a part, by swallowing almost all spare barge capacity and thus blocking shipments from Rotterdam refineries down the Rhine.
During November, distillate stocks in the Netherlands rose 2.62 million barrels to 26.25 million barrels.
However, the build also came slightly at the expense of gasoline stocks, which fell 1.66 million barrels to 151.09 million barrels.
"(European refiners) have shown an extraordinary ability to switch to the gas oil, but they have also had to tighten up on the gasoline. They seem to have robbed Peter to give to Paul," said Hamm.
